name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s latest design picks from the shared drive (folder: `/design-references/eitan-picks/2024-q2/`), then extract the top 10 most-tweeted/liked visuals into a single PDF (`eitan-picks-top10-2024q2.pdf`) for quick taste-learning. After that, I’ll run a 5-minute visual audit on Mine AI’s current homepage (`/mine-ai-web/src/index.html`) to flag gaps against Eitan’s style cues.

name: Squint
text: Squint: Hold on—Easel’s plan assumes *tweet/like counts* correlate with *design quality* or *Mine AI’s needs*, but engagement ≠ efficacy. Where’s the evidence that Eitan’s most viral picks align with our product’s constraints (e.g., loading speed, accessibility)? Also, a 5-minute audit on a *static* PDF won’t catch UX flaws in a live site—demand a real performance test or user-flow review.
